title: Places in town
summary: Name the main places in a city, say where people go, and build a verbal sentence: the verb first, then the subject.
intro: Cairo is huge, and today Daniel finally explores it. You learn the names of places in town, such as مَسْجِد (mosque), بَنْك (bank) and مَتْحَف (museum). You also meet a new kind of sentence, the verbal sentence, which starts with the verb: يَزُورُ السُّيَّاحُ الْمَتْحَفَ (the tourists visit the museum). Notice that the verb stays singular even though the tourists are many.
objectives: Name eight places in a city
Say where someone goes with إِلَى (to)
Build a verbal sentence: verb + subject + object
Keep the verb singular before a plural subject

realLife.title: Saturday in downtown Cairo
realLife.story: It is Saturday and there is no school. Sami offers to show Daniel the centre of Cairo: Tahrir Square, the Egyptian Museum, a bank, a famous old bookshop and, at the end, a green park. Daniel brings a map, a bottle of water and a notebook. On the first page he writes مَدِينَة (city).

sentences.en: The tourists visit the museum every day.
sentences.literal: visits the tourists the museum every day

mistakes.why: When the verb comes first, it stays singular, even before a plural subject.

sentences.en: Cairo is a very big city.
Where is the bank, please? (to a man)
sentences.literal: where (is) the bank, from your kindness

mistakes.why: Layla is a woman, so the verb starts with ta-: tadhhabu.

sentences.literal: prays the people in the mosque

dialogue.title: A walk through downtown Cairo
dialogue.culture: Cairo is often called 'the city of a thousand minarets'. Five times a day you hear الْأَذَان, the call to prayer, from its mosques. In Egypt the weekend is Friday and Saturday, so many schools and offices are closed on both days.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا دَانْيَال! الْيَوْم السَّبْت، وَلَا دُرُوسَ. هَيَّا نَزُورُ وَسَطَ الْمَدِينَة!
lines.en: Good morning, Daniel! Today is Saturday and there are no lessons. Let's visit the city centre!

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور! فِكْرَة مُمْتَازَة. عِنْدِي خَرِيطَة لِلْقَاهِرَة، لٰكِنِ الْمَدِينَة كَبِيرَة جِدًّا!
lines.en: Good morning to you! An excellent idea. I have a map of Cairo, but the city is really big!

lines.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة! أَوَّلًا نَذْهَبُ إِلَى مَيْدَانِ التَّحْرِير، وَهُوَ قَرِيب مِنْ هُنَا.
lines.en: No problem! First we go to Tahrir Square, and it is close to here.

lines.ar: يَا سَامِي، مَا هٰذِهِ الْبِنَايَة الْكَبِيرَة الْحَمْرَاء فِي الْمَيْدَان؟
lines.en: Sami, what is this big red building in the square?

lines.ar: هٰذَا هُوَ الْمَتْحَف الْمِصْرِيّ. يَزُورُ السُّيَّاحُ الْمَتْحَفَ كُلَّ يَوْم.
lines.en: That is the Egyptian Museum. Tourists visit the museum every single day.

lines.ar: أُحِبُّ الْمَتَاحِف! لٰكِنْ أَوَّلًا، أَيْنَ الْبَنْك؟ أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى مَال.
lines.en: I love museums! But first, where is the bank? I need some money.
segs: to (after 'need': no meaning of its own)

lines.ar: الْبَنْك فِي شَارِعِ طَلْعَت حَرْب، وَبِجَانِبِهِ مَكْتَبَة قَدِيمَة وَمَشْهُورَة.
lines.en: The bank is on Talaat Harb Street, and next to it is an old, famous bookshop.
segs: Talaat (part of a street name in Cairo)
Harb (part of a street name in Cairo)

lines.ar: مَكْتَبَة؟ رَائِع! أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْكُتُب. هَلْ عِنْدَهُمْ كُتُب بِالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة أَيْضًا؟
lines.en: A bookshop? Wonderful! I love books. Do they have books in English too?

lines.ar: نَعَم، عِنْدَهُمْ كُتُب كَثِيرَة بِالْعَرَبِيَّة وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة. يَذْهَبُ الطُّلَّابُ إِلَى هُنَاكَ كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: Yes, they have lots of books in Arabic and English. Students go there a lot.

lines.ar: مَا هٰذَا الصَّوْت الْجَمِيل يَا سَامِي؟ هَلْ هُوَ مِنَ الْمَسْجِد؟
lines.en: What is this beautiful sound, Sami? Is it coming from the mosque?

lines.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا الْأَذَان. يَذْهَبُ النَّاسُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِد الْآن لِلصَّلَاة، وَأَنَا أَيْضًا.
lines.en: Yes, that is the call to prayer. People are going to the mosque now to pray, and so am I.

lines.ar: طَيِّب، أَنْتَظِرُكَ هُنَا أَمَامَ الْمَسْجِد. وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْحَدِيقَة؟
lines.en: OK, I will wait for you here in front of the mosque. And after that, shall we go to the park?
segs: I wait for you (to a man)

lines.ar: نَعَم! الْحَدِيقَة قَرِيبَة، وَفِيهَا أَشْجَار كَثِيرَة. تَجْلِسُ الْعَائِلَاتُ هُنَاكَ فِي الْمَسَاء.
lines.en: Yes! The park is close, and it has lots of trees. Families sit there in the evening.

lines.ar: مَا أَجْمَلَ الْقَاهِرَة! أَمَاكِن كَثِيرَة، وَشَوَارِع مُزْدَحِمَة، وَنَاس طَيِّبُونَ.
lines.en: How beautiful Cairo is! So many places, busy streets and kind people.

reading.title: Daniel's notebook
reading.ar: الْقَاهِرَة مَدِينَة كَبِيرَة. فِي وَسَطِ الْمَدِينَة مَيْدَان وَمَتْحَف وَبُنُوك وَمَكْتَبَات. يَزُورُ السُّيَّاحُ الْمَتْحَفَ كُلَّ يَوْم. تَزُورُ الْعَائِلَاتُ الْحَدِيقَة فِي الْمَسَاء. أَنَا أُحِبُّ شَارِعَ طَلْعَت حَرْب.
reading.en: Cairo is a big city. In the centre of the city there is a square, a museum, banks and bookshops. The tourists visit the museum every day. Families visit the park in the evening. I love Talaat Harb Street.
segs: Talaat (part of a street name in Cairo)
Harb (part of a street name in Cairo)

quiz.prompt: Choose the correct verb: '… the tourists the museum.'
Fill the gap: 'Layla goes to the bookshop.'
In the dialogue, what is next to the bank?
How is ج said in Modern Standard Arabic?

completion: Great walk! You can name places in town and build a verbal sentence that starts with the verb.
